label: early/mid original-phase inputs t/d/r/c/y/k/o/i/2/3, boosted when sequence starts with e/n/f/0/z/b/g/q
explanation: 86% of activation mass is in the original (input) phase, peaking at t=2..5 (t=3 has the highest rate, 13.6%). It never fires at t=0 and rarely at the delimiter step or in the early copy steps. It depends on the current input: t, d and r have the highest rates (14-19%), then c, y, k, 3 and 2. It also depends on the first token of the sequence: sequences that start with e, n, f, 0, z, b, g or q raise the rate about 2-2.7x. In the copy phase the same first-token set shows up as out_tok. The strongest activations (near max) are on t, d or r at t=3..5 in sequences that start with e, n or f, often right after an o. Activations are graded and spread out (median 0.078 against a max of 0.39). A context-free version (window plus token set only) scores F1 0.38; adding the first-token condition gives dev F1 0.45, precision 0.41, mass recall 0.67. The remaining activations are a scattered mix of content: some in the late copy phase (recall_idx 5-7) and some on other letters. They looked like a mixed hidden-state direction rather than one clean rule.
